senses.definition: To follow with the eyes; to look in the direction of (someone or something departing).
senses.example: The marshes were just a long black horizontal line then, as I stopped to look after him; and the river was just another horizontal line, not nearly so broad nor yet so black; and the sky was just a row of long angry red lines and dense black lines intermixed.
wordFamily: the devil looks after his own

senses.definition: To seek out, to look for.
senses.example: My subject does not necessarily oblige me to look after this water, or point forth the place whereunto 'tis now retreated.
wordFamily: the devil looks after his own

senses.definition: To care for; to keep safe.
senses.example: He asked me to look after his daughter while he was away.
wordFamily: the devil looks after his own

senses.definition: To have as one's business; to manage, be responsible for.
wordFamily: the devil looks after his own

senses.example: Mens hearts failing them for feare, and for looking after those things which are comming on the earth; For the powers of heauen shall be shaken.
